comments.value:
Anti aliasing should not be used anyway, as the game already has anti-aliasing of its own.

What do you propose as a solution for the screenspace reflections? Moving to the Deferred rendering path would be an extremely bad idea. Deferred is not suitable for VR for many reasons. Having it be selectable by the world creator could be nice, provided that MSAA can be turned off on runtime (which probably isn't very easy).

The other bugs you talked about (Bloom and DoF) are caused by keyword overuse. Unity only has room for 256 keywords in a single session, after which any more can no longer be added. As far as I know, this is not fixable on VRChat's end.
Thank you for reporting this issue. Since this post is quite old, we are requesting that you confirm that the issue is still present and to provide any updated information.

details:
A few bugs associated with Post Processing Stack are happening, I'm not sure when this started appearing but it has pretty much messed up all my worlds as I am a big fan of the Post Processing Stack asset, it allows me and other world creators to bring out the best of their worlds with a few simple effects.

- Anti-aliasing
There's a bug where you get double (or even quadruple) vision when enabling it. This happened to all my worlds, even some of the small simple ones which I can't update at the moment since I don't have access the the files currently. (The files are on my old pc.)

I'm assuming this started with the move to the newer version of Unity.

- Screen Space Reflections
I'll be refering to my old post from Feb 2018 where I talked about this feature and the rendering path required for it. (https://vrchat.canny.io/feature-requests/p/deferred-rendering-path-and-hdr)

This feature is still not functional which is sad considering how amazing this feature is. I'd go as far as saying that this is probably the best feature in Post Processing Stack. This feature enables the ability to have more accurate reflections based then the standard Reflection Probes with little to no performance impact as it's a post processing effect based on what you're seeing on the screen. 

People seem to be miss informed about the required rendering path to make this function, many saying it will be bad for performance while it actually isn't. Defered Rendering actually has a way more predictable performance impact then Forward Rendering, therefore it should also in theory be easier to work with and optimize for. I'm not gonna go too much into detail because it's all documented on Unity's website. (https://learn.unity.com/tutorial/introduction-to-lighting-and-rendering?signup=true#5c7f8528edbc2a002053b52b)

- Bloom
This actually works but there's an odd bug with it currently where the values seem to reset default. Upon entering the world with this enabled, everything seems fine. However, after being gone from the world for awhile and re-entering it, the values seem to have changed, giving an overpowering bloom in most of my own worlds. Can't really tell why this is happening and I'm not sure if this is actually an issue with the asset or something that happens server sided, as it does initially work.

- Depth of Field
Okay, you might wonder why I would even want this for VR in the first place. To explain my situation, I have a world with cameras setup and these cameras are connected to a render texture which then is projected onto a screen. This is where Depth of Field comes into play for me, as these cameras are static and I wanted to have a clear focus on one area in the frame. Now this is very specific use for this and there might not be many other cases where you would wanna use this.

To actually come to the 'bug' I've encountered with this, this feature functions fine initially. Just like the bloom, this seems to either reset to default or turn off completely after coming back to the world at a later state.


These are the bugs I've personally encountered and I have been able to reproduce them. I'm not sure if there's any other bugs related to any of the other features of the Post Progressing Stack as I don't really use the other features outside of Unity's Editor.
title: Post Processing Stack (Bloom, Anti-aliasing, etc)
